title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000029: the validator's safety-requirement verification rule tests the wrong endpoint of the verifies link, so a correctly directed verification link cannot clear the finding it raises

revision_history.description: Corrected the verifies/validates rule in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py to read the link's TARGET endpoint, which is the direction master prompt section 13 declares, and added three self-tests proving both directions: a correctly directed link is not flagged, a requirement with no link is flagged, and a link with the requirement as source does not count as verification. Validator findings fell from 21 to 9; self-tests rose from 11 to 14, all passing. Audited every other endpoint-reading rule and found no further inversion.

evidence: Read from docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py. The rule computes verified = {l['source_id'] for l in links if l.relation_type in ('verifies', 'validates')} and then raises 'safety requirement has no verifies/validates link' for any safety-domain requirement whose id is absent from that set. The master prompt section 13 defines the relation as 'verification measure -> requirement', and the corpus's own convention follows that: the pre-existing finding FB2-REV-FND-000008 states that 'in the corpus's own convention a test measure is the SOURCE and the requirement is the TARGET, so a well-verified requirement appears as a link TARGET, never as a source'. A correctly directed verifies link therefore places the requirement at the target, and the rule, which reads only the source, still reports it as unverified. This was verified on disk after the five security measures were authored: FB2-VER-TMS-000016..000020 each carry a verifies link to FB2-SAF-SEC-000001..000005 respectively, and each requirement is present as a target and absent as a source. The rule's finding count is therefore unchanged by correct work. The same rule is responsible for the seven 'no verifies/validates link' findings against the FSR records, so 12 of the corpus's 21 standing findings come from this single defect.
impact: The corpus's own headline metric for verification coverage is produced by a rule that cannot distinguish a verified requirement from an unverified one. A safety requirement that is fully verified by twenty measures and one that has none score identically. Because the rule under-reports, it under-reports safely: nothing claims coverage it cannot show. But it also means that closing findings FB2-REV-FND-000008..12 is not achievable by doing the work, and a team following the rule literally - adding links in the reversed direction so the rule fires - would corrupt the graph's documented semantics to satisfy a checker.
root_cause: The rule was written as a quick presence check over whichever endpoint was convenient and was never reconciled with the relation's declared direction in the link schema and the master prompt. The mismatch is invisible until someone authors a correctly directed link and observes that the finding does not clear.
resolution:
RESOLVED, and the vocabulary member is corrected from 'accepted' to 'resolved'. Re-verified on 2026-09-30T00:00:00Z by reading the live source: the rule in docs/artifacts/tools/corpus.py builds its set from the link TARGET - `verified = {l["target_id"] for l in links if l.get("relation_type") in ("verifies", "validates") and l.get("target_id")}` - which is the direction master prompt section 13 declares. The defect is gone.

This finding's central claim needs one correction, because it was later found to be the wrong diagnosis of a neighbouring problem and the distinction is load-bearing. This record blamed the endpoint inversion for why findings FB2-REV-FND-000008..12 could not be closed. It could not be closed by the inversion alone. A SEPARATE and independent blind spot sat in the fault_reaction rule (MUT-008), which carried an id filter `"-FSR-" in id` and was therefore structurally incapable of reporting the five FB2-SAF-SEC-* security requirements at all. Both are recorded; the second is FB2-REV-FND-000039 and it was fixed by widening that rule's scope. Had only the inversion been fixed, the security requirements would still have carried no machine-readable fault reaction and the corpus would still have been silently under-reporting.

The rule's fix is unchanged and remains as recorded: the intent is the same - a safety requirement with no verification at all is still reported - and the fix is strictly harder to satisfy by accident than before, because a requirement appearing as the SOURCE of a verifies link is a malformed link under the declared direction and no longer counts as verification. Three self-tests pin both directions. The self-test that pins the negative case was also narrowed in this pass, from 'no rule at all may flag this record' to 'the verification rule may not flag this record', because the former was only true while the fault_reaction rule's id filter hid the same record class; the narrowing makes the test assert what it says it asserts, and MUT-008's coverage of that class is now pinned by four dedicated tests instead. human_approval_status remains pending, production_authorized remains false and product_verification_credit remains false. No human approved this revision, no tool is claimed to be qualified, and no certification, ISO 26262 conformity or ASPICE capability level is claimed or implied.
